key_insight: Taguchi DOE showed that wire feed rate is the dominant driver of tensile strength in GMAW of ST-37 mild steel, with the best response near 26 V, 184.33 A, and 220 m/min.
engineering_relevance: The study gives weld-process engineers a compact parameter recipe for improving joint strength while reducing trial-and-error in production GMAW settings.
method: Used an L9 orthogonal array to test 9 parameter combinations at 3 levels.
Applied signal-to-noise ratio analysis and ANOVA to rank process sensitivity.
Compared the predicted optimum with the best experimental weld result.
evidence_signal: ANOVA assigned 34.64% influence to wire feed rate, 19.42% to welding current, and 5.95% to arc voltage, and the top trial achieved 688 MPa tensile strength.
watch_item: The optimum is based on bead-on-plate tests on ST-37 mild steel, so transferability to other joint geometries, consumables, or materials should be validated before full-scale use.
paper_title: Optimization of Gas Metal Arc Welding Process Parameters for Enhanced Tensile Strength of Mild Steel Weldments Using the Taguchi Design of Experiments and Analysis of Variance
